notes.title: Discover a Cute, Cozy Idle Game Where Pandas Run a Laundromat!
notes.notes:
Our friends at [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/45181686]Destroyer Doggo[/url] have created an adorable and relaxing idle game, [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/3194550/Bao_Baos_Cozy_ Laundromat/]Bao Bao’s Cozy Laundromat[/url]. Step into the world of Bao Bao, the lovable panda, and manage a bustling laundromat with colorful washing machines, dryers, and panda helpers taking care of the shop.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44081746/922e170cc15b932c768bb9dacfea2d59fe500d88.png[/img]

Customize your space with charming decorations like plants, chairs, vending machines, and even adorable cats! Streamers can engage their audience with built-in Twitch chat support, while multitaskers will love the dock mode, perfect for occasional management while working or relaxing.

Discover the cozy charm of [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/3194550/Bao_Baos_Cozy_Laundromat/]Bao Bao’s Cozy Laundromat[/url] today—visit the Steam store page to learn more and grab the game!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/3194550/Bao_Baos_Cozy_Laundromat/

notes.title: Ricochet and Damage Indication - Mechanical Fury Devlog #2
notes.notes:
The pistol rounds are bigger and more prominent. This way its easier to trace the ricochet shots and look really cool. 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44081746/c428b69fceb3b94b5fb2889d4a3231445a88cce5.gif[/img]
It also lets me do this really cool looking orbital strike that one shots all the fodder class enemies.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44081746/1d47a406bce3dc12bbeead649bc8bb4210b106f8.gif[/img]

After a bunch of playtester feedback, there is now a damage indicator that points at the source of damage.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44081746/8365edeaae75f5b5d1d002bbec0d4dae2c8fc1dd.gif[/img]
It gets more intense based on the amount of damage taken, but doesnt become a distraction so that you can start looking for health pickups or just start grapple kicking smaller enemies
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44081746/41e470ffbc74c8d1af9ecced9d64234ae77529c6.gif[/img]

Join the discord to playtest! 
https://discord.gg/E3w6Uzd3GK

notes.title: The Humanoid Mech - Mechanical Fury Devlog #1
notes.notes:
The Humanoid Mech is probably the most powerful enemy in the game.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44081746/2feba1ecfa01e01661ae9a86fd85814af7658661.png[/img]

If you're too far, its gonna shoot projectiles as it closes the gap.

notes.title: Mechanical Fury Devlog #0 - 5 months of work in one post!
notes.notes:
I’ve been working on the game for roughly six months now and I wanted to go over how I went from an empty editor window to a cool steam page! After this I'll move on to really short form updates every week. I gotta get this one out though. 

The first playable I came up with using stock 3D models and animations

[h1][b]Ideation[/b][/h1]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44081746/51a74aaca329d7bed3ff72355aef340e509421e6.gif[/img]
Mechanical Fury started as an experiment in Unreal Engine because I really just wanted to learn to use it. I started making a player character with a grappling hook. While working on it, I came up with the core mechanic of reeling into enemies and kicking them to do extra damage and the idea was too fun not to make into a full game.So, I set up a perforce server and made a detailed excel sheet outlining what I wanted to create, estimated timeframes, and the order of implementation.

[h1][b]Movement System[/b][/h1]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44081746/5c07fda3a2a4d53569dfad6d48074ee3fc329cbc.gif[/img]
Inspired by games like Dusk and Celeste, I focused on creating a platforming experience with tight controls. The grappling hook along with the movement system and resulted in intuitive controls. With playtesters' feedback, I also ended up adding wallrunning. However, this introduced a significant challenge, which I will address in the level design section.

[h1][b]Enemies[/b][/h1]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44081746/883bff93df5d4ef2579e8e9766633c17fad98852.gif[/img]
Based on the design document, there are 13 enemy types categorized as Fodders, Heavies, Mini-bosses, and bosses, similar to Doom Eternal. Currently, only the fodder enemies are implemented, that you can destroy for ammo and health. There are three fodders:
[*] Punchybois (melee attackers)
[*] Shootybots (ranged attackers)
[*] Splodies (suicidal enemies)
Whatever they do is in the name itself!

[h1][b] Weaponry[/b][/h1]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44081746/fa507c443154545de0c2265765faa37c6a1457ac.png[/img]
There are 6 weapons that have a regular fire and an alt fire that activates when the player kicks the bullets:
[list]
[*] A Revolver whose bullets can be kicked to make them ricochet
[*] A Quad Barrel Super Shotgun that can be kicked for an explosive shot
[*] A Rambo-style Gattling gun which can be kicked to shoot homing bullets
[*] A Grenade Launcher that can be kicked into a Rocket Launcher
[*] A Crossbow that spins like a beyblade when kicked, slicing all enemies in its way!
[*] And finally the Railgun, a reference to my other game Kickback! It can literally one shot anything in its way!
[/list]

[h1][b]Level Design[/b][/h1]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44081746/207eb1f11245d62326294838427ab6ef9409cd9f.gif[/img]
With the foundational elements in place, I delved into level design. With a ton of playtester feedback, I was able to create the whitebox of a proper first level. However, I faced a challenge as the player could only move upwards, making downward movement feel like a fail state. To address this, I introduced a slide system, allowing players to dive downwards and slide under surfaces. Paired with a progressively vertical movement system, it opened up a really engaging level design mantra. 

I encourage everyone interested to join the Discord community and become an Aviator! I post regular builds and updates there!

See y'all next time!
